items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...until after the War there were a lot of guys came out of Detroit like Milt Jackson... [INTERVIEWEE] And they were the fore...they were not the forerunners, they were the aftermath of the exodus, shall we say.

ctx.x: Well, I'll take a look and see. If they were taped, we should have them.

Yeah. But anyway, we had...we really had some...we had Milt Jackson and they had a cross section of people, you know. James P. Johnson, Mahalia Jackson and any person you name, they had up there. And sometimes, you know, you have to make records of activities, much against the will of the person, but in the end it may prove to be the history. I know that for any number of years I wouldn't allow writers to put my discography in their books, 'cause they wasn't giving me any of it...I'm commercial, you see, and I…

And when a guy go out and give an assignment to go write...to write and assignment, they more than likely, if he has any brains, will give him some money to get picture rights, or to get the right to use the name, something...and I just don't think that people should use your material like that in the public domain. If that's the case, then why do we have the copyright laws? Why do we have, you know what I mean, laws of patent offices? And why do we have...so that you can restrain a person from using your…
